result.title: Scoring Higher, Answering Worse: Mitigating Reward Hacking in Rubric-Based RL via Protocol-Level Rubrics
result.summary: Rubric-based reinforcement learning (Rubric-RL) trains language models where no verifier exists. A judge checks each criterion of a rubric, and the verdicts are aggregated into a reward, most often by a weighted sum. We show that this additive aggregation is the weak point. Under a sum, criteria compensate for one another: a policy that misses the one decision that matters can buy the points back with advice nobody asked for. On clinical consultation, such a policy scores higher and answers worse. Rubric coverage rises while appropriateness on held-out physician criteria falls below the untrained model. The medical criteria are not to blame. Grouped so that they must hold together, the same criteria, unchanged to the word, recover a third of the loss; shorter answers recover almost none. We therefore propose Protocol-level Rubrics (ProRubric), which keeps what the criteria ask for and changes how they are aggregated. It groups a checklist into a few protocol-level dimensions. A dimension counts only when all of its criteria hold and its failure clause does not fire. The grouping is done once, offline, and leaves the optimizer unchanged. ProRubric raises appropriateness by 10.8 points without losing coverage and has the best seven-benchmark average at both scales. Reward validity is set not only by what a rubric verifies, but by how it aggregates. Code is available at https://github.com/Estrellajer/ProRubric

AI.brief_summary: 论文发现基于评分表（rubric）的 RL 中，加权求和式聚合会让条目互相补偿，导致「分数更高、回答更差」的奖励劫持；为此提出 ProRubric，将清单离线分组成少量协议级维度，维度内全部条目成立且失败条款未触发才计分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心论点——奖励不仅取决于「验证什么」，还取决于「如何聚合」——可能为 LVR 中答案对 latent 内容的贡献分配与验证/停止决策提供一个可核查的聚合设计视角，但与视觉或多模态推理无直接联系。
